tweet.text:
I’ve run the experiment. If I give an agent a big ball of mud, and ask it to make a change, it will spin and thrash hopelessly. If I give an agent a nicely partitioned and clean project, I can ask it to make changes all day long, and it has no trouble.

The rules that I find to be most useful are intense test coverage, three strands of tests: unit tests, acceptance tests, and QA tests.  Small well named functions (although not as small for agents as for humans.) Well partitioned modules. Appropriate dependency structure. And the keen eye of the supervising human doing spot checks over all of it.
